core.title: A component URN follows the stack's component URN shape (profile: urn.component)
core.given: A component URN is involved, in any artifact
core.when: you write, build, reference or store it
core.then: It must match the stack's component URN shape (profile: urn.component) exactly: every prescribed segment present in order — owning product capability id, owning feature id, logical component name, deployment side, architectural layer — joined only by the shape's hierarchy separator, with no missing or extra segment, and conforming to the stack's canonical pattern for that shape (segment casing and the accepted side and layer values included).
prefer: {capability} = the owning product capability's id; {feature} = the owning feature's id; {name} = the logical component name; {side} = the deployment side (one of the side values accepted by the stack's component URN shape); {layer} = the architectural layer (one of the stack's layer roles).
User/system flow infrastructure: product capability id 'user/system flows', and its layer is always the composition root.
Product capability entrypoints: feature id 'product capability'.

A feature-composition component sits above the standard layers; the rule mandates neither its layer nor its name — the reference example uses the composition-root layer and the name 'composition', both illustrative only.
avoid: A separator other than the URN shape's hierarchy separator between segments, or a missing or extra segment.
core.why: A stable, uniquely-shaped URN ties each component to its owning product capability and feature and fixes its deployment side and architectural layer, so the graph can address components unambiguously.
evidence: Every component URN involved matches the stack's canonical component URN pattern (profile: urn.component), including segment casing and the accepted side and layer values.
{capability} resolves to a real product capability and {feature} to its owning feature.
verification: A check matches every component URN in scope against the stack's canonical component URN pattern (profile: urn.component): exact segment count and order, only the shape's hierarchy separator between segments, and every accepted spelling of a side value (full and abbreviated forms) is valid.
Scope: any component URN, in any artifact kind (plan artifacts, source code, tests, tooling, docs); copies and references get no exemption.

The pattern check does not by itself establish that {capability} resolves to a real product capability and {feature} to its owning feature (the rule's evidence additionally requires this). The check mandates neither a particular layer nor a particular name for feature-composition components (the composition-root layer and a name like 'composition' come only from the reference example), while the always-composition-root layer for user/system flow infrastructure stays mandatory.

values: component URN string added, edited, copied or referenced

fires: A component URN appears in any artifact: plan artifact, manifest, plan model, acceptance, doc, source, test or tooling.
A component URN is created, edited, copied, referenced or stored.
doesNotFire: No component URN is involved (for example, only product capability or feature URNs).

profileRequirements.meaning: The exact grammar of a component URN in this stack: scheme prefix and segment order (owning product capability, owning feature, component name, deployment side, architectural layer), the hierarchy separator, segment casing, and the accepted side and layer values; every component URN in any artifact must match the canonical pattern.
The stack's architectural layer roles, whose local names are the accepted values of the {layer} segment.

The stack's local name for the composition-root layer: the {layer} value always required for user/system-flow-infrastructure components. For feature-composition components it appears only in the reference example, not as a requirement.

bunOnly.reason: Names the ATDD-Bun utility that constructs component URNs (utils.graph.URNBuilder.component(capability_id, feature_id, component_name, side, layer)); other stacks build URNs differently, so the neutral core activates on generic component-URN task terms only.

Concrete example URN of the reference realization; the core keeps only the role-level guidance (user/system flow infrastructure, composition-root layer) because bun.json is delivered as the worked example.

Concrete example URN of the reference realization; the core keeps the concept (feature composition above the standard layers) without repeating the example, and without turning the example's layer or name into a requirement.

neutralityNotes: The URN scheme itself is planner-scheme level, not stack-specific, so it stays in the core: the component prefix and segment roles, the special ids 'user/system flows' (user/system flow infrastructure, whose layer is always the composition root) and 'product capability' (product capability entrypoints), feature composition above the standard layers, and the requirement that {capability}/{feature} resolve to real owning artifacts. Everything concrete about the grammar — the hierarchy separator ':', segment casing, the accepted side spellings (frontend|backend|fe|be), the layer names, and the canonical pattern a URN must match — is profile data (urn.component, roles.layers, roles.composition_root.name), so another stack can supply its own shape without changing the obligation. No new profile key was needed: the accepted side values are part of the component URN shape itself (urn.component), and layers already have roles.layers. The only stack-specific content is the URNBuilder.component builder symbol in the activation task terms and the concrete example URNs, which remain in the reference realization. Faithfulness notes: the Bun canonical pattern permits dots in the {name} segment, and bun.json's agent-facing text states no separate no-file-extension rule, so the core deliberately adds none. The feature-composition example's layer (the composition root under Bun) is kept illustrative only: the core requires that layer solely for user/system flow infrastructure, exactly as bun.json does; it does not mandate any layer or name for feature-composition components.
